fichas.title: Underpinning Existing Adjacent Buildings
fichas.summary: When a new building is erected beside an existing building whose foundations are higher, the existing foundations must be underpinned to reduce the risk of settlement or ground failure. The work requires careful design, planning, construction, and site supervision. Minor deformation may still occur; a pre-work survey is recommended.
uses: Support existing foundations during adjacent excavation and construction
Reduce the risk of settlement or ground failure

dimensions.label: Settlement of underpinned building
dimensions.context: Settlement up to this amount is generally considered unavoidable.
dimensions.ocr_raw: Fine cracking and settlement of the underpinned building by up to 5 mm is generally considered unavoidable.

fichas.title: Groundwater Control for Building Excavations
fichas.summary: Excavations below the water table require groundwater management. Open dewatering pumps water from sumps, trenches, and drains; closed dewatering lowers groundwater with underwater pumps. Where lowering the water table could affect nearby soil or buildings, the excavation bottom may need waterproofing, supported excavation walls, and an underwater concrete or grouted base.
uses: Create a waterproof base where groundwater lowering is unsuitable

dimensions.label: Safety distance under excavation base
dimensions.context: Approximate safety distance for lowering groundwater using underwater pumps under the excavation base.
dimensions.ocr_raw: the groundwater is lowered using underwater pumps (with a safety distance of about 50 cm) under the base of the excavation.
